title: every-non-cognition-ticket-crosses-to-buildme-in-one-batch
intention: Every ticket whose work needs no cognition crosses to BUILDME in one batch, so nothing that could already be built is left short of the build door when Fable is let go.

decisions.text: Instrument repaired to current names, same claim measured: the harbor map reads where each ticket stands today, not whether it crossed in the batch (0853294fe972 was retreated to TICKETME on 2026-10-14 for an unrelated proven_by fix), so C1 reads the journal: 'cd ~/dev/src/CairnCommons && python3 tickets/0682e51ab011-batch-measure.py' — every history.json in both roots, a forward BUILDME row for each of the seven dated 2026-09-07 whose entry_gate read a berthed chart chain claiming the ticket; 7 of 7, 14:21:12-14:27:35, exit 0. The negative control (25ee4866642e in place of 201a37bf1613) reads 6 of 7, exit 1. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'.

The forward BUILDME names --proven-by /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/tickets/0682e51ab011-batch-measured.md only, the piece the quorum seal is over (validation CairnCommons/tickets/validations/0682e51ab011-batch-measured.json, signer Akien 'APPROVED THRU PROVED. FASTEST ROUTE TO EVERYTHING PROVED', notary cc; open-83ff98f1ef31 answered 'a) Yes: CC signs and seals concept-pieces from now on'). The 2026-09-07 BUILDME was never journaled in either root and named no proof. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'.

The ticket owns no code; its owning_intention is intentions-not-beside-code/_charter+why.json, so its crossings journal at CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code (history.json, state.json) — the same berth 728d393d70ed's crossings already use. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'.

VOYAGE MECHANICS: 'cairn rehearse 0682e51ab011' runs until it exits 0 before anything crosses. Every crossing is 'PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m cairn.tools.base.cross 0682e51ab011 <STAGE> --actor cc --why <one line> --proven-by /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/tickets/0682e51ab011-batch-measured.md', and clearance.clear runs inside that call; the builder never calls it directly. BUILDME --why: '0682e51ab011: concept-piece — batch measured'. PROVEME --why: 'the piece sealed; every validate criterion ran green by its instrument'. The verdict comes from cairn.devices.codemother.machines.verdict.verdict.write_verdict: one entry per validate criterion with claim verbatim, instrument, outcome 'pass', evidence and discriminating_observation set to that instrument's printed output, and every hypothesis dispositioned confirmed or killed with its deciding observation. Then cross PROVED with --why naming the verdict, then 'cairn rehearse 0682e51ab011 --proved /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/tickets/0682e51ab011-batch-measured.md', commit both repos by exact path (ticket, its .log.jsonl, rehearsals/0682e51ab011-*.json, .artifact-journal.jsonl), and push. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'.

Verified with ls 2026-10-14: CairnCommons/tickets/0682e51ab011-batch-measure.py, 0682e51ab011-batch-measured.md and validations/0682e51ab011-batch-measured.json all exist and are committed; nothing is written. Every verdict entry has expect_exit 0 and timeout_s 1800; they are not read from anywhere else. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'.

The decompose lack (no writes_to) was the re-chart's own packet; writes_to now names tickets/0682e51ab011-batch-measured.md and the chart berthed through validate (validate-20261112T073253-c7fc77a6bf61).
